rows.04:28a0:
"Got it?!
Don't you dare rat on us!"
".............................."
Akasaka didn't answer any more after that.
"Hey, Toru.
That's enough.
He's out cold."
If one of them hadn't stopped him, Hatanaka would have kept on beating Akasaka.{p}
rows.04:2234: Say that and I'll tell the seniors on you
rows.04:2f7c: Decided to just bury the body
rows.04:2fac: Carried him to a futon and laid him down
rows.04:307c:
That night, after everyone was asleep, they buried Akasaka's body.
In secret.
Running away was the last thing on their minds now.
"Where'd Akasaka go?!"
Even when the seniors yelled, they all just put on innocent faces and cocked their heads.
"...He looked like he was having a hard time.
I bet he ran off."
And that satisfied everybody.
He'd been on the list of likely dropouts from the start, after all.
Some of the seniors even nodded like they were glad.
Pretty smug of them, huh?{p}
rows.04:346c:
A search party went out.
But they didn't find him.
Hatanaka and the others were scared out of their minds about what would happen if the body turned up.
Even so, nothing was found, and the search was called off.
After that, Hatanaka and the rest didn't have a care in the world.
They forgot all about Akasaka in no time.
...And then a year went by.{p}
rows.04:1350:
At the start, there are about forty new members.
The tough training cuts that down to about half.
And then comes the summer Hell Camp.
The twenty or so who somehow made it that far get whittled down to five at this camp.
Bet that surprised you, huh?
But those five are strong, let me tell you.
After all, they're the five who survived the Hell Camp.
Their guts are on a whole other level.
They're the ones who carry the boxing club's tradition and pass it on.{p}...So, do you want to know what goes on at that camp?
rows.04:0d2c:
...It's the boxing club.
Boxing's great.
It's a man's sport.
It's the kind of sport a woman can't really understand, right?
People who don't get boxing say it's just a slugfest, just a brawl, but that's dead wrong.
You'd be hard pressed to find a more gentlemanly sport anywhere, don't you think?
Our school's boxing club was really something back in the day, too.
It showed up at the nationals pretty much every single year.
And it placed near the top in a whole bunch of weight classes.
Pretty impressive, isn't it?{p}
